Title: Ardh Metal-Lined Kulhad
Description:
A reusable kulhad concept that keeps the tactile irregularity of fired clay while introducing a removable stainless-steel liner at the drink interface.

Material split

The upper drinking vessel is a thin 18/8 stainless insert. A high-fired earthenware lower shell creates grip, visual weight and the familiar flared kulhad silhouette. The two materials meet below the lip so the mouth contacts polished steel rather than a brittle clay edge.

Why it exists

The insert can be removed for cleaning or replacement while the clay shell remains the expressive object. A dry mechanical seat, high-temperature silicone isolation ring or other food-safe decoupling method should be tested rather than permanently bonding materials with different thermal expansion.

Service mode

Designed as a compact 140 ml chai cup for table service, tasting menus and hospitality sets. The metal half is the hygienic, repeatable component; the earthenware half carries variation and provenance.

Concept-spec notice: Capacity, food-contact materials, joint system, drop resistance, glaze migration, thermal shock and dishwasher performance are unverified prototype targets.

Title: Ardh Clay-Lined Kulhad
Description:
A reusable kulhad concept with a food-contact clay bowl suspended inside a protective metal lower chassis, preserving the clay drinking experience while making the base serviceable.

Material split

A glazed or vitrified earthenware upper bowl forms the entire lip and beverage surface. A spun stainless lower half wraps the vulnerable foot and provides a stable service base.

Replaceable body

The clay insert is conceived as replaceable after breakage, while the metal base remains in circulation. The connection should be reversible and visually expressed as a precise waist rather than disguised as a monolithic cup.

Hospitality logic

The product turns breakage into a component event instead of total product loss, creating a parts-led service model suitable for restaurants and tea programmes.

Concept-spec notice: The vessel is not microwave-safe because of the metal base. Joint retention, glaze safety, washability and thermal performance require testing.

Title: Rekhā Laser-Marked Serving Platter
Description:
A high-fired serving platter whose decoration is generated by selectively laser-marking a tested ceramic surface instead of printing a surface graphic.

Laser field

A radial contour map moves from dense micro-lines at the centre to wider spacing at the rim. The pattern can encode batch, maker or recipe data while remaining visually quiet.

Surface strategy

Two development routes are preserved: mark a compatible glaze to create tonal contrast, or engrave a controlled unglazed exterior zone. The food-contact face should not be deeply ablated until cleanability and glaze integrity are proven.

Service use

The 34 cm format is intended for bread, shared dishes and tableside plating. A broad low profile makes the laser pattern legible at rest.

Concept-spec notice: Laser wavelength, power, mark depth, glaze chemistry, micro-cracking, stain resistance and food-contact suitability require coupon tests before product use.

Title: Rekhā Laser-Marked Chai Bowl
Description:
A 220 ml tea bowl with a narrow laser-marked band that behaves like a material watermark rather than applied decoration.

Etched register

A 12 mm exterior band carries repeated linear notation, batch index and an optional machine-readable serial. The interior remains smooth and fully glazed.

Hospitality detail

The foot is recessed so the bowl can be carried on a small metal service tray without the pattern contacting the table.

Personalisation

The same geometry can support venue editions or room-number sets without changing the clay tool.

Title: Forge Relay Dual-Mass Skillet
Description:
A lightweight searing pan that uses two material behaviours instead of forcing one metal to perform every job.

Working body

A thin nitrided carbon-steel bowl provides direct, responsive searing and a seasoning-capable cooking surface.

Thermal ring

A removable cast-bronze outer ring seats around the lower wall as a heat reservoir and tabletop trivet. Removing it restores a lighter line-cook mode; fitting it slows temperature loss for table service.

System logic

The ring is not represented as a permanent bonded layer. Keeping it mechanically separate makes cleanability, repair and contradictory thermal behaviours explicit.

Concept-spec notice: Nitriding, bronze alloy, fit tolerance, hot handling, induction behaviour and food-contact boundary require engineering validation.

Title: Forge Split-Field Plancha
Description:
A plancha concept that physically divides two cooking materials across one continuous service object.

Steel zone

Two-thirds of the surface is nitrided carbon steel for high-heat searing, browning and scraping.

Bronze service zone

A raised cast-bronze end platform is thermally coupled but isolated from direct food contact by a removable stainless tray. It holds cooked items, sauces or garnishes while the steel zone remains active.

Hospitality choreography

The pan moves from twin-burner cooking to tableside finishing without becoming a decorative serving board disconnected from the cooking process.

Concept-spec notice: This speculative assembly requires validation for differential expansion, flatness, safe lifting, induction coverage and removable-tray hygiene.

Title: Forge–Terre Nested Roaster
Description:
A low roasting vessel built as a stainless cooking tray nested inside an earthenware presentation cradle.

Metal insert

A removable fully-clad stainless insert performs oven roasting, deglazing and induction-compatible sauce finishing.

Clay cradle

A laser-marked high-fired ceramic cradle receives the hot insert at the table, protecting surfaces and converting cookware into a composed serving object.

Replacement logic

Either component can be replaced independently. The clay piece never goes on the hob and the metal insert can be cleaned without soaking the ceramic body.

Concept-spec notice: The ceramic cradle is not cookware. Clear thermal, dimensional and misuse constraints must be validated and encoded.

Title: Kuro Strip 200 Chef's Knife
Description:
A thin 20 cm chef knife concept formed from a single continuous strip of steel, with the handle architecture exposed rather than hidden under scales.

One material path

A laser-cut and forged strip runs from tip through heel, spine and open handle loop. The loop creates a visible counter-curve and keeps the knife unmistakably metal rather than imitating a conventional riveted handle.

Grip interface

A removable textured sleeve clips onto the lower handle rail while the spine rail stays exposed for visual continuity. Sleeve geometry, balance and fatigue are treated as service parts.

Blade intent

A thin, plain-edge blade targets precise push and draw cuts. It is not positioned for bones, frozen food or twisting loads.

Concept-spec notice: Steel grade, heat treatment, distal taper, weld-free feasibility, balance, fatigue and sanitation require prototyping.

Title: Kuro Trace 180 Hybrid-Edge Knife
Description:
A thin 180 mm chef-format slicer with fine scallops limited to the forward two-thirds of the edge, leaving a plain heel for board contact and controlled chopping.

Serrated field

Shallow, widely spaced micro-scallops are proposed for tomatoes, citrus, pastry and soft-skinned produce. This is not a bread-knife saw profile.

Plain heel

The final 60 mm remains a conventional sharpenable edge for herbs, onions and close board work.

Serviceable geometry

The serration pitch, depth and handedness are explicit schema fields because they determine sharpening method and use suitability.

Concept-spec notice: Edge geometry is a test target. The product must not claim universal chef-knife performance or “never needs sharpening” until abrasion and resharpening trials are complete.

Title: Kuro Trace 150 Micro-Scalloped Utility Knife
Description:

Fine scallops

A shallow single-sided micro-scallop pattern is proposed for ripe tomatoes, citrus, sausages and sandwich assembly.

Strip handle

The exposed continuous-metal frame carries a removable grip web, reducing permanent mixed-material joints.

Hospitality role

Compact reach and low blade height suit garde-manger, breakfast and pass stations where large chef knives are excessive.

Concept-spec notice: Handedness, scallop geometry, sharpening, edge life and commercial sanitation remain test items.

Title: Forge–Terre Service Tongs
Description:
A pair of service tongs using spring steel for force and removable fired-clay thumb pads for thermal tactility and table presentation.

Metal skeleton

A continuous spring-steel strip supplies flex, alignment and cleanable food-contact tips.

Clay interfaces

Laser-marked ceramic pads clip onto the handle zone only, staying clear of food and allowing replacement after chips.

Use case

Designed for bread, pastry and plated garnish service rather than high-force grill work.

Concept-spec notice: Pad retention, chip containment, wash cycles and spring fatigue must be tested before hospitality use.
